_readme: Single source of truth for the Rust<->Python API parity guarantee. Rust side: otspot-py/tests/api_manifest_rust.rs (compile-time symbol references + invocation of every listed method on real oracle problems; #[non_exhaustive] Rust enums can only guarantee variant-removal detection, not variant-addition, per Rust's own forward-compat contract for that attribute) plus otspot-py/otspot_model_api_snapshot.txt + scripts/check_otspot_model_public_api.sh (a `cargo public-api` snapshot diff, catching additions/removals of ANY pub item, not just the ones this manifest already tracks). Python side: otspot-py/tests/test_api_manifest.py (introspection of the built `otspot` extension module, both directions: manifest subset of module, and module public surface subset of manifest).

model_error_exceptions._note: otspot_model::ModelError has no Python type of its own: each variant maps to a distinct exception class (Python has no Result type), all subclassing otspot.OtspotError. ModelError::NotSupported has no entry here (see out_of_scope): it is unreachable from any bound Python call.

entries.note: carries a `.error: otspot.SolveError` attribute (see methods.SolveFailedError below)

Model.note: new otspot-model getter added alongside this PR so VarKind is reachable, mirroring var_name
runs under Python::detach (GIL released for the duration of the solve)

Variable.note: replaces the constraint! macro, which Python has no equivalent of

ModelResult.note: uses try_value internally, raises InvalidInputError instead of panicking on misuse

SolveFailedError.note: attribute holding the real otspot.SolveError instance, attached via setattr (see errors.rs doc comment: a #[pyclass(extends=PyException)] field needs Py_3_12 under abi3, but this crate targets abi3-py39)

python_only_variants._note: Variants that exist on the Python side but are not real Rust variants -- always the honest fallback for a #[non_exhaustive] Rust enum's mandatory wildcard match arm (see enums.rs's From<Rust> for Py* impls), never an invented capability. SolveStatus's Unknown carries the original Display text (a complex enum can hold a payload); SolutionProof/SolveError's Unknown is payload-less (eq_int enums cannot carry one) but is still a distinct, honest 'not one of the known variants' value rather than panicking or silently aliasing a real variant.

out_of_scope: otspot_model::ConstraintSense (variants Le/Ge/Eq) - Constraint's fields (including `sense`) are pub(crate) with no public getter anywhere in the Rust API (unlike Variable's kind, exposed via the new Model::var_kind), so a Python binding would be a decorative type nothing ever produces or consumes. Re-add if/when otspot-model grows a constraint introspection API.

ModelError::NotSupported / a hypothetical NotSupportedError - only produced by the QCQP/SOCP bridge (see the conic entry below), which is out of scope; the variant is unreachable from any call this crate binds.
otspot_core::conic::* (QCQP/SOCP/MISOCP solve_socp/solve_qcqp/etc.) - not bound in v1; Model.add_qc_le/add_soc_le are not exposed

otspot_core::problem::{LpProblem, QpProblem} raw construction and otspot_core::lp::solve_lp_with / otspot_core::qp::solve_qp_with raw entrypoints - Python uses otspot_model::Model exclusively, the crate's own recommended high-level entrypoint

Model::try_add_var / try_add_int_var / try_set_timeout - eager-Result variants of add_var/add_int_var/set_timeout, which already defer validation errors to solve() in Rust (they never panic), matching the bound Python methods' behavior exactly; no separate try_* binding adds anything

Model::try_var_name / try_var_kind / ModelResult::try_value - eager-Result variants of the panicking var_name/var_kind/value/__getitem__; the bound Python var_name/var_kind/value/__getitem__ use these try_* variants internally already (see errors.rs) and raise InvalidInputError on Err instead of letting the panic through, so no separate try_* binding is needed

Expression::from_constant - a convenience constructor equivalent to passing a bare Python float wherever an Expression is expected; every binding's coerce() dispatch already accepts a bare float uniformly, so a separate constructor call has no use in Python

ModelResult.stats (otspot_core::problem::SolveStats) - internal routing/timing diagnostics (SolveRoute enum, per-phase microsecond timings, warm-start counters, ~10+ fields); binding it would also require binding SolveRoute and is disproportionate scope for this PR

otspot_core::options::SolverOptions / MipConfig / GlobalOptimizationConfig / BranchingStrategy / etc. (incl. SolverOptions::with_tolerance) - only the subset reachable through Model's set_* methods (timeout, tolerance, presolve, threads, obj_offset) is bound

otspot_core::qp::ipm_solver::outcome::IpmOutcome::infeasibility / infeasibility_status - internal IPM solver machinery (constructs a diagnostic outcome from a SolveStatus), not part of any path reachable from Model

otspot.InternalError - mapped from ModelError::Internal, a solver-internal invariant violation (e.g. validate_qp_dual_len's length-mismatch guard); not a documented, deliberately-triggerable failure mode from well-formed Python calls, so unlike the other 5 model_error_exceptions it has no dedicated behavior-parity test
